variable_coverage.construction: Source definition: Proportion of zero daily stock-return days out of all potential trading days in a fiscal year. Source definition: Binary indicator for a firm that voluntarily switched to IFRS before local authorities announced plans to require IFRS reporting; coded one when the definition applies to the firm-year and zero otherwise. Formula/construction: 1 if the firm voluntarily switched before the announcement; 0 otherwise..

Source definition: Binary indicator for a firm that voluntarily switched to IFRS after local authorities announced plans to require IFRS reporting but before reporting became compulsory; coded one when the definition applies and zero otherwise. Source definition: Interaction of Early Voluntary with Mandatory. Mandatory equals one for firm-years ending on or after the local IFRS adoption date; this interaction captures the incremental period-specific capital-market effect for early voluntary adopters once IFRS is required for all firms in the economy. Formula/construction: Early Voluntary × Mandatory, where Mandatory = 1 for fiscal years ending on or after the local IFRS adoption date..

Source definition: Interaction of Late Voluntary with Mandatory. Mandatory equals one for firm-years ending on or after the local IFRS adoption date; this interaction captures the incremental period-specific capital-market effect for late voluntary adopters once IFRS is required for all firms in the economy. Formula/construction: Late Voluntary × Mandatory, where Mandatory = 1 for fiscal years ending on or after the local IFRS adoption date..

Source definition: Binary indicator for firm-years ending on or after the local mandatory IFRS date for firms that have never previously reported under IFRS; mandated observations of voluntary IFRS adopters are excluded. Formula/construction: 1 for qualifying first-time mandatory firm-years; 0 otherwise..

Source definition: Binary indicator for financial reports following U.S. GAAP, based on Worldscope field 07536 and adjusted for contradicting coding identified by manual review of annual reports. Source definition: Binary indicator for firms traded on a technology or other high-growth exchange whose listing rules mandate or allow IFRS reporting. Source definition: Natural logarithm of the annual standard deviation of monthly stock returns, lagged one year. Formula/construction: ln(Return Variability_{t−1}); Return Variability = annual standard deviation of monthly stock returns..

variable_coverage.construction: Source definition: Measured daily return on security j used in the transaction-cost threshold system; the latent true return is shifted by the estimated negative- or positive-information threshold or observed as zero within the no-trade region. Formula/construction: R_jt. This is an assigned supporting-model input used to construct a baseline measure; retain its fit and all raw components.

Source definition: Daily equal-weighted return on the home-country market index, used in the latent true-return market relation for each security. Formula/construction: R_mt. This is an assigned supporting-model input used to construct a baseline measure; retain its fit and all raw components.

Source definition: Natural logarithm of the yearly estimate of round-trip transaction costs. In Appendix A.3, latent true returns follow a market relation and observed returns are censored by estimated negative- and positive-information transaction-cost thresholds; the measure is the estimated upper threshold minus the lower threshold. Formula/construction: ln(α₂ⱼ − α₁ⱼ). The baseline dependent variable is a generated result of its frozen supporting fit; the raw requirements above supply the fit inputs.

variable_coverage.construction: Source definition: Firm-year average of four implied cost-of-equity estimates from the Claus–Thomas, Gebhardt–Lee–Swaminathan (GLS), Ohlson–Juettner–Nauroth (OJ), and Easton modified PEG models. Each estimate is the internal rate of return that equates the stock price with its model-specific expected sequence of residual income or abnormal earnings. CT uses forecast EPS and beginning-of-year book value through T=5, clean-surplus book-value forecasts and a constant payout fraction; terminal residual income grows at expected inflation, proxied by the annualized country-specific median of one-year-ahead realized monthly inflation. GLS uses three explicit forecast years, then linearly fades forecast ROE toward the historic three-year average ROE in a country-year within Campbell industries; negative yearly target returns are replaced by country-industry medians, and residual income is constant from T=12. OJ combines one-year-ahead EPS and dividends with short-term growth equal to the mean of forecast EPS growth from years 1 to 2 and the I/B/E/S five-year growth forecast, and long-term growth equal to expected inflation; a positive forecast earnings change is required. Modified PEG uses one- and two-year-ahead EPS and year-1 dividends, assumes abnormal-earnings growth persists, and requires positive forecast earnings changes including reinvested dividends. Required inputs are the current price, mean analyst EPS forecasts for years 1 and 2, and either year-3 EPS or long-term growth; missing year-3-to-5 EPS forecasts are filled recursively using long-term growth, and missing long-term growth is imputed from the forecast EPS change from years 2 to 3. Prices and mean forecasts are measured at month +7 after fiscal year-end; prices are shifted to the beginning of the fiscal year for full-year discounting. Forecast dividends use the firm’s historic three-year payout ratio, with the country-year median substituted when missing or outside [0,1]. Long-run inflation growth is country-specific; negative inflation is replaced by the country historical median over 1980–2005. IRRs are solved iteratively until imputed and actual prices differ by at most 0.001; only positive estimates are retained. Formula/construction: mean(r_CT, r_GLS, r_OJ, r_PEG).

Cost of Capital is the average cost of capital estimate implied by the mean I/B/E/S analyst consensus forecasts and stock prices using the Claus and Thomas [2001] model, the Gebhardt, Lee, and Swaminathan [2001] model, the Ohlson and Juettner-Nauroth [2005] model, and the Easton [2004] model.

For each model, we substitute market price and analyst forecasts from I/B/E/S into the valuation equation and back out the cost of capital as the internal rate of return that equates current stock price and the expected future sequence of residual incomes or abnormal earnings. We average over the four models to obtain a single estimate per firm-year observation.
We assume clean surplus, that is, future book values are imputed from current book values, forecasted earnings, and dividends. Dividends are set equal to a constant fraction of forecasted earnings.

At time T = 5, it is assumed that (nominal) residual income grows at rate g equal to the expected inflation. As a proxy for g, we use the (annualized) median of country-specific, one-year-ahead realized monthly inflation rates.
After the explicit forecast period of three years, the residual income series is derived by linearly fading the forecasted accounting return on equity to the industryspecific median return.

We compute the historic three-year average return on equity in a given country and year based on the industry classification in Campbell [1996]. Negative yearly target returns are replaced by countryindustry medians. From T = 12 on residual income is assumed to remain constant.

Following Gode and Mohanram [2003], the short-term growth rate, gst, is estimated as the average between the forecasted percentage change in earnings from year t +1 to t +2 and the five-year growth forecast provided by financial analysts on I/B/E/S.

The model embeds the assumption that growth in abnormal earnings persists in perpetuity after the initial period. Note that it requires positive changes in forecasted earnings (including reinvested dividends) to yield a numerical solution.
OJ long-run abnormal-earnings growth g_lt equals expected inflation, the annualized country-specific median of one-year-ahead realized monthly inflation.

Move the month+7 price back to beginning fiscal year with the imputed cost of capital, then use full-year discounting, equivalent to partial-year discount factors.
Dividend payout is each firm’s historic3year average; if missing or outside[0,1], substitute the country-year median payout.
Long-run terminal growth uses annualized country-specific median one-year-ahead monthly inflation; negative values are replaced by historical country inflation median over1980-2005.
We stop iterating if the imputed price falls within a 0.001 difference of its actual value. Implied cost of equity capital estimates are restricted to be positive and set to missing otherwise.
